scope.mode: read-only architectural audit; this receipt is the only new file

finding.smallest_additive_leq_78: Encode every fixed dependency on device, but retain the CPU router decision as the only mid-token boundary. The flagship has 75 sparse layers, so schedule one command segment from one sparse router to the next and one final segment through lm_head/sampling: 75 + 1 = 76 waits/token. This does not require all-expert residency because the CPU can admit and bind the eight selected experts after each route wait.
finding.leq_3_requirement: Eliminate the 75 CPU route boundaries. A GPU-produced expert id cannot select a Rust Buffer from the current name-based LRU. It requires a stable GPU-addressable table or contiguous expert bank for every possible expert used by the graph, plus a selected-expert PQ kernel or GPU-encoded ICB. ICB alone does not make absent or evictable resources addressable.
finding.replay_requirement: MTLCommandBuffer is one-shot. Replay needs persistent scalar/resource argument buffers and an ICB (or a true persistent causal kernel), with all indirect resources kept alive at stable addresses. The repository has scalar KernelArgBuffer support and one raw gpu_address megakernel pattern, but no GLM resource argument table and no ICB implementation.

flagship_schedule.conditionality: matvec_into creates a boundary only for PQ/device-BF16 tensors; NativeCpu runs synchronously on CPU. Conversely, matvec_batch can create more physical command buffers than its single manual wait tick when a batch contains NativeGpuBf16 calls, because those dispatch synchronously one by one before the PQ batch.
flagship_schedule.counter_conflict: estimate_resident_waits_per_token reports 583 because it charges dense MLP as two waits, but batched_mlp unconditionally invokes and counts gate, up and down as three waits. The 66.1%-unattributed promoted profiler and its reported 234 synchronizations are therefore not a complete physical-command count.

dormant_kernel_audit.metal_registration: gravity_pq.metal is concatenated into all_shader_sources and compiled into the single library. MetalContext::pipeline resolves any function lazily by string, so no explicit registration table blocks use.
dormant_kernel_audit.trace_registration: static_kernel_name maps only gravity_silu_mul_f32, gravity_axpy_f32, gravity_add_inplace_f32 and gravity_pq_matvec. Every other resident kernel below would be recorded as 'other' until the trace table is extended.

dormant_kernel_audit.capacity_conflict: ActPool hard-codes idx_scores to 8192 floats while the CPU path writes pos+1 scores. Position 8192 requires 8193 floats and the unchecked write_f32 becomes an out-of-bounds write. Move sequence-sized score/selection scratch into the growable ResidentSession before any 8K/32K gate.

changes: Count physical submits/waits in MetalContext, not hand-maintained logical ticks; fix the 583-vs-586 estimator/test.
Add every dormant resident kernel to static_kernel_name.
Add repr(C) parameter mirrors, encode-only wrappers that always accept a caller TokenCommandBuffer, and tiny frozen parity fixtures.
Move all sequence-sized scratch out of the fixed 8192 ActPool allocation.

implementation_sequence.goal: <=78 waits/token without dynamic GPU expert selection
changes: Upload norms/biases once and use the existing RMSNorm, RoPE, KV append, query build, DSA/top-k, sparse-attention, residual, zero and axpy kernels.
Preallocate expert gate/up/act/down/combined scratch; do not allocate buffers inside the token loop.

Encode one segment through each sparse router, wait, run the existing CPU router_select unchanged, admit/bind the eight chosen experts, then encode their MLP plus all fixed work through the next sparse router.
After the last router wait, encode its experts, remaining residual/final norm, lm_head, argmax and top-5 in one final segment.
Keep DSA top-k and final expert/token choices exact under Numeric Parity V2.1; retain a near-tie replay fallback rather than silently changing a choice.
Replace name-based selected-expert binding with a stable per-layer expert resource table or contiguous packed expert bank plus offsets.
Add exact GPU noaux_tc routing and a selected-expert PQ gate/up/down kernel that indexes the bank using device expert ids.
Keep every indirectly referenced Buffer alive and mark it useResource(Read); current 32-GiB LRU eviction is incompatible with stable raw addresses.
Encode three 26-layer command buffers with GPU ordering and only a final CPU-visible wait; prove three-CB and one-CB results identical.
Prebuild persistent resource/scalar argument buffers and an ICB after warmup.
Update only token id, position, sequence length and cache offsets per token; execute the fixed ICB, then read token+diagnostics.
No allocation, pipeline creation, cache admission, tensor-name lookup or CPU decision is permitted after replay begins.

dynamic_expert_boundary.current: router_select reads 256 logits on CPU, constructs eight expert names, and ensure_many_locked admits those exact buffers. Their identities do not exist until after the router projection wait.
dynamic_expert_boundary.argument_buffers: A true resource table or raw-GPU-address table lets a kernel index expert resources by device expert id, but all referenced resources must have stable lifetime and be declared with useResource.
dynamic_expert_boundary.ICB: Useful for replaying the fixed dispatch sequence. It solves dynamic selection only if GPU code encodes commands/bindings, or if fixed commands call a selected-bank kernel. Pre-encoding 256 experts with predication preserves decisions but reads/launches too much and must be rejected on measured bytes/time.
dynamic_expert_boundary.all_expert_residency: Current source documents about 82 GB for the full routed artifact. Added to the measured 11.7 GB promoted resident set, this is about 93.7 GB before KV, scratch and OS headroom on a 96-GB host, so naive physical residency is not viable unless a measured no-copy/addressable bank avoids swap and page-fault churn.
dynamic_expert_boundary.cpu_boundary: Keeping the current CPU router is sufficient for 76 waits. It is mathematically incompatible with <=3 on a 75-sparse-layer model.

inputs.units: decimal GB; derived floors are optimistic

roofline.interpretation: At 6.89 GB/token, command collapse alone cannot reach TG2/TG1: even one CB has an optimistic 9.58-ms additive floor. At complete geometry, one CB is still about 3.72 ms. Reaching TG2/TG1 therefore also requires fewer active bytes and/or more effective bandwidth/compute efficiency; wait count is not sufficient.

conflicts: Source-exact logical schedule is 586, but the frozen estimator asserts 583.
The promoted profiler reports 234 synchronizations while 66.1% of the token is unattributed; it cannot falsify the source schedule or establish a physical-command count.
GPU_EXPERT_WAVE reduced the MLP drain estimate but measured 1413 ms versus the promoted 828 ms; it is a correctness building block, not a promotable implementation.
The dormant kernels are compiled but almost wholly unwired and untested; most would trace as 'other'.
The fixed 8192-score allocation is incompatible with the required 8K/32K sustained gates.
The 32-GiB LRU and evictable per-tensor buffers conflict with stable all-expert GPU addresses and graph replay.

Kernel arithmetic uses parallel reductions, explicit fma and Metal exp where the host uses different reduction/transcendental implementations; continuous parity alone is insufficient at DSA/router decision boundaries.
exact_falsifiers: Production-mode physical tracing on the same warmed token reports anything other than 76 waits for the route-segment implementation, or any synchronous dispatch occurs inside an encode-only helper.
Any layer differs from the host oracle in DSA top-k, router expert ids/order, normalized expert weights, final greedy token or diagnostic top-5.
The near-tie fallback cannot restore and replay the pre-layer residual/KV state exactly.
Position 8192 or a 32K run allocates/writes beyond sequence scratch, reallocates after warmup, or changes a prior KV/index key.
The route-segment path is not faster than the 828-ms promoted baseline over a replicated complete-token run; wait reduction alone is not promotion.
Serial gravity_glm_stable_topk_f32 or thread-0 sparse attention consumes enough GPU time to erase the fixed-cost saving at 2K, 8K or 32K.

All-expert addressing exceeds memory headroom, evicts a resource whose GPU address is in an argument table, faults/swaps during steady state, or reads materially more than the eight selected experts plus the shared expert.
The <=3 path performs any CPU expert selection, name lookup, cache admission or buffer rebinding between its first and last command buffer.
Replay creates a Buffer/pipeline/command sequence after warmup, changes a resource GPU address, or cannot execute the same ICB for successive positions.

Measured effective bandwidth or non-overlapped fixed overhead makes any roofline floor higher than the optimistic values above; the roofline may be falsified only upward, never used as achieved latency.
